supplements.scope: Task-local definitions, proved transformations, resource counts, hardware calibration, numerical checks and exploration budget
supplements.content: Exact rational semantics for finite FP64 inputs, effective single-CPU compute/stream calibration, a conservative 32768-byte fast-storage budget, payload-based two-level resource counts, and at most 12 candidate evaluations. Full specification is in ../SPECIFICATION.md and remains pending user confirmation.
supplements.basis: User-selected CPU fusion and tiled matrix multiplication experiments; C baselines and Model.lean; ../environment.json and calibration sources. Reference traffic is an idealized payload model, not measured DRAM transactions.

specification.description: Preserve y[i] = (a[i] * b[i] + c[i]) * d[i] while reducing three full-array passes and two slow-storage intermediates to one fused pass.

specification.semantics: Exact rational multiplication, addition, multiplication in that order. C uses separate FP64 operations with contraction disabled. Formal resource comparison is for n=4194304; additional measured sizes are 1024 and 262144.
conditions: Inputs and outputs are disjoint, contiguous, row-major FP64 arrays on the CPU; allocation and initialization are outside timing.
Lean checks exact rational operations. Runtime rounding and compiled-code correctness are checked separately; neither is established by the mathematical proof.
The cost model counts idealized two-level payload traffic. Cache hits, write allocation, prefetch, associativity, vectorization, loop overhead, and scheduling are not modeled.
Compute and bandwidth fields are the effective measured rates in ../environment.json, not advertised peaks. The field name hbm_bytes denotes modeled slow-level payload bytes on this CPU.
The fast-storage budget is 32 KiB, a conservative working budget within the guest-reported 48 KiB L1 data cache; it is a model assumption, not an enforced cache partition.

Baseline payload is 3 * 24*n bytes and 3*n FLOPs; fused payload is 40*n bytes and 3*n FLOPs. Scalar live-value budgets are 24 and 40 bytes respectively. All input and output payload is charged at the modeled slow-storage boundary.
